name: Acute bacterial conjunctivitis
summary: Engorged superficial vessels worst toward the fornices and palest at the limbus, sticky discharge, puffy lids; cornea clear, pupil normal.

revealed_by.diffuse: Fiery red eye from engorged, mobile superficial vessels, worst in the fornices and corners and paler toward the limbus; lids slightly puffy; creamy mucopurulent strands in the lower meniscus and a pool at the inner corner.
revealed_by.optic_section_cornea: Clear cornea of normal thickness and a quiet, deep anterior chamber: the inflammation stays on the surface.

teaching_points: Conjunctival injection is worst away from the limbus; a ciliary flush is worst at it and points to the cornea, iris or angle.
Vision, pupil and cornea are normal; any of them abnormal means it is not simple conjunctivitis.
Mucopurulent discharge that glues the lids in the morning suggests bacteria; watery discharge suggests a virus or allergy.
Most cases settle in 5-7 days; topical antibiotics shorten them. Refer if vision falls, the eye is painful or it does not settle.

provenance.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology, 9th ed.; AAO Preferred Practice Pattern: Conjunctivitis (2023). Values render-calibrated.
